concepts.name: Neural Oscillations
concepts.short_description: Rhythmic brain activity at multiple frequencies; gamma binding, theta sequences, cross-frequency coupling.

concepts.name: Topology
concepts.short_description: Study of properties preserved under continuous deformations; connectedness, holes, and invariants.

concepts.name: Wavelet Transforms
concepts.short_description: Multi-resolution time-frequency analysis; localized basis functions, multiresolution analysis, denoising.

identity is relational (phase difference), not absolute

dynamics: none intrinsic; dynamics enters as a path through a space of configurations

locality: local moves cannot change global invariants

invariants: vanishing moments: blindness to polynomials below order p

hypotheses.statement: Topologically protected phase memory: in a ring of coupled oscillators the winding number of phase around the loop is an integer that can change only by a phase slip; the ring stores integers robustly, and wavelet-localized phase is the readout that sees slips as local transients.

Binding by cross-scale persistence: features of an input that keep the same connected-component structure across several wavelet scales are the ones an oscillator population locks together; synchrony implements the persistence selection of a filtration.

Nested rhythms as a dyadic address space: slow-phase / fast-cycle nesting is a multiresolution ladder, and the topology of the nesting (tree of octaves vs torus of incommensurate rhythms) sets how many items can be addressed and how addresses fail.

Defect bookkeeping as computation: in a 2D oscillator medium phase singularities carry integer charge; computation is creation, motion and annihilation of charges under a conservation law, with wavelets localizing each event in time and scale.

Learning as surgery: the coupling graph changes its cycle structure when wavelet coherence between units crosses a threshold at some scale; learning events are exactly the moments the graph's Betti numbers change, and new cycles create new places to store windings.

Deformation-invariant timing: a code written in phase relative to a carrier is invariant to monotone warps of time (homeomorphisms of the time axis) because the carrier warps along with the message; wavelet phase tracking is what makes the reference co-moving.

Drift immunity through vanishing moments: a readout built from wavelets with p vanishing moments ignores polynomial phase drift below order p, so an oscillator code need only protect the non-polynomial part of its phase; topology decides which part cannot drift away (the integer part).

Winding-number memory: a closed ring of identical phase oscillators with nearest-neighbour coupling holds twisted states whose integer winding q is a stored value; q changes only via a phase slip on one link, so retention time is set by the slip barrier, not by the per-unit noise.

concept_contributions.Neural Oscillations: the phase variable on S1 and the locking that makes twisted states attractors
concept_contributions.Topology: the closed loop that makes q an integer invariant
concept_contributions.Wavelet Transforms: local instantaneous phase readout at each node from noisy observations

knockouts.Neural Oscillations: no phase variable, no winding; memory would need a separate bistable mechanism
knockouts.Topology: on an open chain with free ends the twist relaxes to synchrony; q is not defined
knockouts.Wavelet Transforms: weak: phases could be read directly in simulation; the wavelet only matters when units are observed through noisy signals

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: local gradient stiffness: each link independently holds a phase difference 2*pi*q/N, and retention is just the per-link escape rate (a Kramers problem), with the loop playing no role beyond fixing the boundary condition

questions.what_exists: N phase oscillators on a cycle graph
questions.what_is_selected: twisted states with small local gradient (low |q|/N)
questions.what_can_reproduce: q can be copied by entraining a second ring
questions.what_can_learn: nothing learns in the base mechanism
questions.what_can_transfer: q transfers to any closed-loop substrate (2D torus, spin ring)
questions.distinguishing_observable: retention time of q in a ring vs a pinned-end chain holding the same local gradient

hypotheses.statement: Slip-ridge repair: a phase slip appears as a localized discontinuity in the wavelet ridge of the two nodes adjacent to the slipping link; a local controller that detects the discontinuity and injects an opposite slip restores q without any global knowledge.

concept_contributions.Neural Oscillations: slips are the only way the stored state is lost
concept_contributions.Topology: the error is an integer jump, so correction is exact, not approximate
concept_contributions.Wavelet Transforms: time-scale localization of the discontinuity lets a local detector find it

knockouts.Neural Oscillations: no slips to correct; noise acts continuously
knockouts.Topology: without the loop a slip is not an error (no invariant to restore)
knockouts.Wavelet Transforms: detection would need the full global phase field instead of a local time-frequency test

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: periodically re-imposing the target phase profile from an external copy (refresh), which needs global knowledge but no detection

questions.what_changes: q under noise, corrected by injections
questions.what_can_transfer: the detect-and-inject-opposite rule to any integer-charge system
questions.distinguishing_observable: retention gain versus a twin that injects the same number of corrections at random times and links

hypotheses.statement: Cross-scale persistence binding: two locations of an input are coupled (and therefore synchronize) only if they fall in the same connected component of a superlevel set of the scalogram at k or more of the dyadic scales; synchrony clusters then equal the scale-persistent components.

concept_contributions.Neural Oscillations: synchronization turns graph connectivity into shared phase that can be read out downstream
concept_contributions.Topology: connected components and their persistence across a filtration
concept_contributions.Wavelet Transforms: the multiscale family over which persistence is measured

knockouts.Neural Oscillations: the result could be read as graph components with no dynamics; oscillators only add a readout (knockout may be weak)
knockouts.Topology: without component structure there is nothing to be persistent
knockouts.Wavelet Transforms: a single scale reverts to ordinary thresholded segmentation

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: multiscale smoothing followed by thresholding and connected-component labelling, with no oscillators

questions.what_exists: input signal, scalogram, coupling graph, oscillators
questions.what_persists: component membership that survives k scales
questions.what_can_learn: k and threshold could be adapted
questions.what_can_transfer: the persistence rule to 2D images or graphs
questions.distinguishing_observable: cluster agreement of the cross-scale rule vs a single-scale rule with matched edge count

hypotheses.statement: Dyadic nesting address: a slow rhythm with f_slow and fast rhythm with f_fast = 2^d f_slow form a d-level address tree; the number of reliably addressable slots grows as 2^d until phase noise in the slow cycle exceeds a slot width, giving a capacity cliff at a predictable d.

concept_contributions.Neural Oscillations: the nested rhythms and phase-amplitude coupling
concept_contributions.Topology: circle-of-circles structure (a torus when ratios are incommensurate, a tree when dyadic)
concept_contributions.Wavelet Transforms: the dyadic ladder that defines the address levels

knockouts.Topology: if the nesting is incommensurate the address space becomes a torus with no clean slots; weak but real
knockouts.Wavelet Transforms: the dyadic choice is arbitrary; any integer ratio would give a similar cliff (weak dependency)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: a fixed-size buffer with k slots set by the ratio of two timescales; capacity cliff from ordinary timing jitter

questions.what_is_selected: items that lock to a slot
questions.what_can_transfer: capacity law to any two-clock system
questions.distinguishing_observable: capacity vs d follows 2^d up to a cliff whose location scales with slow-phase noise

hypotheses.statement: Warp-invariant phase code: message symbols are coded by phase relative to a carrier that is carried along with the message; any monotone time warp applied to the transmission leaves carrier-relative phase unchanged, so decoding by wavelet-tracked carrier phase is invariant to tempo changes that break clock-time decoding.

concept_contributions.Neural Oscillations: the carrier rhythm acting as a co-moving reference
concept_contributions.Topology: monotone warps are homeomorphisms of the time line; order and relative position are what survive
concept_contributions.Wavelet Transforms: adaptive-scale phase tracking follows the carrier when its local frequency changes

knockouts.Topology: weak: the topological framing adds vocabulary; the invariance is just a shared reference frame
knockouts.Wavelet Transforms: a fixed-frequency Hilbert or FFT phase estimate breaks under strong warps

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: any shared co-warped clock (e.g. a sync pulse each cycle) gives the same invariance; nothing oscillatory or topological is needed

questions.what_is_selected: codes that use relative rather than absolute timing
questions.distinguishing_observable: decoding accuracy under warp for carrier-phase vs clock-time decoders

hypotheses.statement: Coherence-triggered surgery: an edge is added between two oscillators when their wavelet coherence exceeds c* at some scale for T steps and removed when it falls below c_low; the cycle rank of the coupling graph therefore grows with the number of independent rhythmic co-occurrences in the input, creating new loops that can hold windings.

concept_contributions.Neural Oscillations: the coherence that drives the rule
concept_contributions.Topology: Betti-1 of the coupling graph as the learned quantity
concept_contributions.Wavelet Transforms: scale-resolved coherence decides at which scale co-activity counts

knockouts.Neural Oscillations: no coherence signal, the rule never fires
knockouts.Topology: without tracking cycles the rule is ordinary Hebbian wiring
knockouts.Wavelet Transforms: a single-band coherence would miss co-occurrences at other scales

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Hebbian correlation-based wiring; loops appear only as a side effect of edge density

questions.distinguishing_observable: cycle rank vs number of independent input rhythms, compared to degree-matched random rewiring

hypotheses.statement: Betti-matching pressure: in a population of oscillator networks selected on a task needing M integers of memory, selection favours networks whose coupling graph has cycle rank at least M; wavelet energy penalties at unused scales push the rest of the graph to be tree-like.

concept_contributions.Topology: cycle rank as the resource count
concept_contributions.Wavelet Transforms: the scale-energy penalty shaping the rest of the graph

knockouts.Topology: without the loop resource the pressure has no target
knockouts.Wavelet Transforms: without the penalty graphs just stay dense (weak dependency)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: selection for any memory capacity yields more recurrent connections; loop count is a correlate of edge count

questions.what_is_selected: graphs with the right cycle rank
questions.distinguishing_observable: cycle rank tracks M while edge count is held fixed by constraint

hypotheses.statement: Vanishing-moment drift immunity: a phase readout using wavelets with p vanishing moments is exactly blind to polynomial phase drift of order below p, so an oscillator code subjected to slow polynomial frequency drift remains decodable, while the integer part (winding) is protected separately.

concept_contributions.Topology: the integer part that cannot drift
concept_contributions.Wavelet Transforms: vanishing moments define what the readout ignores

knockouts.Topology: weak: the drift immunity works without any loop; topology only names the non-drifting part
knockouts.Wavelet Transforms: the central role; without it the drift corrupts decoding

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: detrending with a polynomial fit before decoding

questions.distinguishing_observable: decoding error vs drift order crosses a step at order p

hypotheses.statement: Defect-charge logic: in a 2D lattice of phase oscillators, vortices of charge +1/-1 are tokens; pair annihilation implements a subtraction and charge conservation guarantees the net count survives any smooth perturbation; wavelet transients at the core mark each event.

concept_contributions.Topology: charge as an integer invariant and its conservation
concept_contributions.Wavelet Transforms: event localization in time and scale

knockouts.Wavelet Transforms: weak: plaquette winding sums detect cores without wavelets

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: counting particles in a reaction A + B -> 0 with diffusion; the oscillator medium only supplies the particles

questions.distinguishing_observable: net charge conserved under noise while total defect count decays

hypotheses.statement: Scalogram Reeb graph as trace: the merge tree of level sets of a network's output scalogram records when rhythms split and merge; distinct computations produce distinct merge trees even when their power spectra match.

concept_contributions.Neural Oscillations: the rhythms that split and merge
concept_contributions.Topology: Reeb graph / merge tree of level sets
concept_contributions.Wavelet Transforms: the time-scale plane whose level sets are taken

knockouts.Topology: without topology this is just a spectrogram
knockouts.Wavelet Transforms: without the transform no plane to take level sets of

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: comparing spectrograms directly with a distance metric

questions.what_exists: output signals and their merge trees
questions.what_can_transfer: as a descriptor to any time series
questions.distinguishing_observable: classification of computations by merge tree beyond spectrogram distance at matched power spectrum

hypotheses.statement: Homotopy-only relay: oscillator layers at frequencies f, 2f, 4f couple only between adjacent octaves and only through a coarse phase sign; what passes between scales is the winding class, not the phase value, so coarse layers constrain fine ones only up to homotopy.

concept_contributions.Topology: the winding class as the transmitted quantity

knockouts.Topology: without restricting to class the relay passes full phase (ordinary coupling)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: quantized coupling: a 1-bit channel between layers

questions.distinguishing_observable: mutual information between layers bounded by log2 of number of classes

hypotheses.statement: Shrinkage-feedback dynamics: the network's activity is repeatedly wavelet-transformed, soft-thresholded and fed back; small components die and persistent structures survive, so the dynamics performs topological simplification in real time.

knockouts.Topology: without persistence the effect is just denoising

questions.distinguishing_observable: features removed ranked by persistence, not by amplitude alone

hypotheses.statement: Slip mutation: in an evolving population of rings, mutation inserts a single phase slip (q -> q +/- 1) rather than perturbing weights; heredity of q is exact between mutations and the mutation spectrum is discrete.

questions.distinguishing_observable: fitness landscape over q is discrete-stepped

hypotheses.statement: Length-protected lifetime: retention time of winding q grows with ring length N at fixed q because the per-link gradient 2*pi*q/N shrinks; protection is local stiffness scaled by the loop's length.

knockouts.Topology: without the loop no total twist

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Kramers escape over a per-link barrier

questions.distinguishing_observable: lifetime depends on N only through q/N

hypotheses.statement: Wavelet-kernel coupling: oscillators coupled through a Mexican-hat kernel in space form phase domains whose number is set by kernel scale; the domain count (Betti-0) is a scale-selected integer.

knockouts.Topology: weak: domain count is a detail
knockouts.Wavelet Transforms: kernel could be any lateral inhibition shape (weak)

questions.distinguishing_observable: domain count vs kernel scale follows an integer staircase

lenses.name: Winding ledger
lenses.rationale: Invented for this triplicate: if memory is an integer carried by loops, the natural record is a ledger of windings per independent cycle and of every slip event.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: phase time series of all nodes plus the cycle basis of the coupling graph
lenses.transformation: sum wrapped phase differences around each basis cycle each step; record jumps as slip events with link and time
observables: slip count and location per unit time
predictedSignals: q piecewise constant with rare jumps
slip locations concentrated where local gradient is largest
lenses.nullExpectation: for random or unlocked phases q performs a random walk with frequent jumps
failureModes: ambiguity when a link sits near pi
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: gives the integer state directly instead of inferring it from correlations

lenses.name: Scalogram persistence barcode
lenses.rationale: Invented: turn the scalogram into a stack of filtrations so binding can be compared with persistence directly.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: continuous wavelet scalogram |W(s,t)| at 6 dyadic scales
lenses.transformation: superlevel-set 0-dimensional persistent homology per scale, then link components across scales
observables: number of components surviving k scales
predictedSignals: true objects persist across >= k scales, noise bumps do not
lenses.nullExpectation: for power-spectrum-matched phase-randomized surrogates, bar length distributions match the object-free case
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: quantifies the persistence side independently of the oscillator dynamics

lenses.name: Slip-ridge coincidence
lenses.rationale: Invented: tests whether time-frequency events and topological events are the same events.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: wavelet ridges of each node's observed signal plus the winding ledger
lenses.transformation: detect ridge phase discontinuities above a jump threshold; match to ledger slips within a time tolerance
observables: precision and recall of ridge-detected slips vs ledger slips
predictedSignals: precision and recall >= 0.8 at moderate observation noise
lenses.nullExpectation: for time-shuffled ridge events the coincidence rate equals the chance rate set by event density
failureModes: ridge discontinuities from amplitude dips not slips
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: connects the measure concept to the structure concept causally, not only by vocabulary

lenses.name: Barrier accounting (statistical mechanics)
lenses.rationale: Stock lens used to expose M1 as possibly a familiar Kramers mechanism.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: retention times across N, q, coupling K, noise D
lenses.transformation: fit log mean lifetime vs K/D and vs q/N
observables: slope of log lifetime on K/D
collapse of curves when plotted vs q/N
predictedSignals: if protection is purely local, curves for different N collapse on q/N
lenses.nullExpectation: no collapse would mean the loop contributes beyond local gradient
failureModes: finite simulation time censors long lifetimes
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: decides whether 'topological protection' is more than local stiffness

lenses.name: Time-warp gauge
lenses.rationale: Invented: treat monotone time warps as a gauge freedom and ask which decoders are gauge invariant.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: encoded symbol streams before and after random monotone warps
lenses.transformation: apply piecewise-linear warps of strength w and decode with carrier-phase and clock-time decoders
observables: decoding accuracy vs w for each decoder
predictedSignals: carrier-phase decoder flat in w, clock decoder falling
lenses.nullExpectation: if the carrier is not warped with the message, both decoders fall together
failureModes: warps strong enough to fold cycles into each other break any decoder
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: separates invariance due to a co-moving reference from invariance due to the code itself

lenses.name: Cycle-rank budget
lenses.rationale: Graph-theoretic accounting of how many independent loops a network has versus how many integers it must hold.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: coupling graph snapshots over learning or evolution
lenses.transformation: compute cycle rank E - V + C and compare with task memory demand M and edge count
predictedSignals: performance tracks cycle rank at fixed edge count
lenses.nullExpectation: performance tracks edge count and cycle rank is irrelevant
failureModes: edge count and cycle rank are coupled unless constrained
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: separates loop resources from connection density

lenses.name: Charge audit
lenses.rationale: Invented for defect media: a bookkeeping check that a conservation law actually holds under noise.
lenses.transformation: compute plaquette windings; sum charges in bulk and flux through the boundary
predictedSignals: net charge changes only by boundary flux
lenses.nullExpectation: no conservation in an unlocked random field
failureModes: plaquette winding ill-defined at high noise
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: tests whether tokens are robust enough to compute with

experiments.hypothesis: A closed ring retains winding q longer than a chain whose two ends are pinned to hold the same total twist, at matched local gradient; if not, 'topological protection' reduces to local stiffness.
experiments.mechanism: Noisy Kuramoto ring dtheta_i = K[sin(theta_{i+1}-theta_i)+sin(theta_{i-1}-theta_i)]dt + sqrt(2D)dW, initialized in twisted state q.
experiments.intervention: vary topology: ring vs pinned-end chain (end phases clamped at 0 and 2*pi*q*(N-1)/N) vs free-end chain; vary N in {32,64,128} with q scaled to keep q/N fixed, and D in {0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4}
experiments.control: free-end chain with the same N and K (twist relaxes; lower bound)
experiments.positive_control: ring at D=0 must retain q for all steps in 100% of seeds
experiments.observable: first-slip time and final q from the winding ledger (L1)
experiments.success_criterion: at the D where pinned-chain median first-slip time is between 10% and 90% of the run, ring median first-slip time >= 2x pinned-chain median (bootstrap 95% CI of ratio excludes 1) in >= 2 of 3 N values
experiments.failure_criterion: ring/pinned-chain lifetime ratio CI includes 1 at all N, or log-lifetime curves for different N collapse on q/N within 10% (then the mechanism is local stiffness, M14 wins)
experiments.alternative_explanation: pinned ends are an artificially strong boundary condition that stabilizes the chain more than the ring's loop does, masking any loop effect
experiments.null_twin: pinned-end chain: same N, same per-link gradient and noise, same number of coupled links minus one, loop removed
experiments.why_this_implementation: a 1D phase ring is the smallest system with a winding invariant; no learning substrate is needed
experiments.size: N in {32,64,128}; 3 topologies; 4 noise levels; 20000 Euler-Maruyama steps dt=0.05; 20 seeds
stupid_explanations: the ring has one more coupled link than the pinned chain
pinned ends inject or absorb slips at the boundary, inflating chain slip rate
retention differences come from integration step size near pi

experiments.hypothesis: A local controller that detects slips from wavelet ridge discontinuities in node signals and injects an opposite slip raises q retention beyond a twin making the same number of random injections.
experiments.mechanism: ring of W1 (N=64, q=3) observed only through x_i = cos(theta_i) + observation noise sigma=0.3; complex Morlet at the natural frequency gives phase; a ridge-phase jump > pi/2 between neighbours within 20 steps triggers injection of -sign(jump)*2*pi across that link
experiments.intervention: controller on vs off, D in {0.2,0.3,0.4}
experiments.positive_control: oracle controller reading true wrapped differences (upper bound)
experiments.observable: fraction of seeds with final q equal to initial q; ridge-vs-ledger precision/recall
experiments.success_criterion: retention(wavelet controller) - retention(random twin) >= 0.25 at D=0.3 over 40 seeds (Fisher exact p < 0.01) and detection precision and recall >= 0.8
experiments.failure_criterion: retention gain over random twin < 0.1, or precision < 0.5 (controller creates slips)
experiments.alternative_explanation: injections act as a generic stiffening kick regardless of timing
experiments.null_twin: random-injection controller: same count and sign distribution of injections, placed at random links and times
experiments.why_this_implementation: tests error correction on an integer invariant with only local information; a trained NN detector would displace the explicit time-frequency test that is the point
experiments.size: N=64, q=3, 3 noise levels, 20000 steps, 40 seeds, 4 controller conditions
stupid_explanations: the controller just prevents slips by adding energy
retention measured at a single end time hides slips that were corrected by chance
observation noise level chosen so the wavelet trivially sees everything

experiments.hypothesis: Coupling by cross-scale persistence makes oscillator synchrony clusters match true objects better than single-scale coupling with the same edge count, and better than reading graph components without dynamics.
experiments.mechanism: 1D signals of length 1024 with 3 localized objects at different widths plus 1/f noise; 64 oscillators on a location grid; edge if same superlevel component at >= k=3 of 6 dyadic scales; Kuramoto dynamics 2000 steps; clusters by PLV > 0.9
experiments.intervention: coupling rule: cross-scale (k=3) vs finest-scale only with random edges added/removed to match edge count
experiments.control: phase-randomized surrogate signal with the same power spectrum (objects destroyed)
experiments.positive_control: noise-free signal with well separated objects: ARI >= 0.95
experiments.observable: adjusted Rand index (ARI) between sync clusters and ground-truth objects; ARI of plain connected components of the coupling graph
experiments.success_criterion: median ARI(cross-scale) >= 0.7 and exceeds matched single-scale twin by >= 0.2 (paired Wilcoxon p < 0.01, 50 seeds) AND ARI(oscillators) > ARI(graph components) + 0.02
experiments.failure_criterion: ARI gap to twin < 0.1, or ARI(oscillators) <= ARI(graph components) + 0.02 (then oscillators add nothing and M3 reduces to segmentation)
experiments.alternative_explanation: coarse scales simply smooth noise; any low-pass filter would do the same
experiments.null_twin: single-scale rule with degree-matched rewiring: same edge count and degree distribution, persistence criterion removed
experiments.why_this_implementation: a persistence filtration over a wavelet stack with an explicit phase readout; a GNN segmenter would displace the persistence mechanism under test
experiments.size: signals n=1024, 6 scales, 64 oscillators, 2000 steps, 50 seeds, 3 conditions
stupid_explanations: cross-scale rule just has larger components because coarse scales merge everything
PLV threshold tuned to the favoured condition
objects placed so their widths align with dyadic scales

experiments.hypothesis: Carrier-relative phase decoding is invariant to monotone time warps only when the carrier is warped together with the message; the invariance comes from the co-moving reference, not from the code.
experiments.mechanism: 5 symbols per slow cycle coded by phase slot relative to a 6 Hz-like carrier; transmission warped by random piecewise-linear monotone maps of strength w; decoder tracks carrier phase with an adaptive-scale Morlet ridge
experiments.control: clock-time decoder assigning slots by elapsed time since cycle onset
experiments.success_criterion: carrier-phase accuracy at w=0.4 >= 0.9 with drop from w=0 <= 0.05, AND clock decoder drop >= 0.3, AND in the null twin carrier-phase drop >= 0.3
experiments.failure_criterion: carrier-phase drop > 0.1 at w=0.4, or null twin shows the same invariance (then the result is an artifact of the decoder)
experiments.alternative_explanation: any shared co-warped clock gives invariance; the oscillation is incidental
experiments.null_twin: carrier generated unwarped while the message is warped: same spectra and symbol counts, co-moving reference destroyed
experiments.why_this_implementation: signal-level toy with a hand-built decoder isolates the reference-frame question
experiments.size: 200 sequences x 20 cycles per condition, 4 warp levels, 10 seeds
stupid_explanations: monotone warps preserve order so any order decoder is invariant
warps too weak to move symbols across slot boundaries
adaptive-scale decoder overfits the warp family
